subject: maths
title: Short Sides & Real Problems
welcome_lead: Now you'll rearrange Pythagoras to find a missing short side, and tackle ladders, rectangles and other word problems.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Pythagoras' Theorem — finding a missing short side and applying the theorem to ladders, rectangles and word problems.
final_note: You can rearrange a² + b² = c² to find any side, and apply it to ladders, diagonals and 2D word problems.

concepts.def: b² = c² − a²; subtract instead of add.
Ladder is the hypotenuse; ground & wall are short sides.
Hypotenuse must be the largest number.
Always square-root at the very end.

walkthroughs.body_html:
If you know the hypotenuse and one short side, you subtract to find the other:

b² = c² − a²

Example: hypotenuse = 13, one short side = 5. Find the other.

b² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144. So b = √144 = 12.

Notice this is the 5-12-13 triple again. The biggest number is always the hypotenuse — if you ever get a negative under the square root, you've mixed up the sides.

Classic problem: a 10 m ladder leans against a wall. Its foot is 6 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?

The ladder is the hypotenuse (c = 10). The 6 m ground distance is one short side (a = 6). The wall height (b) is the unknown.

b² = 10² − 6² = 100 − 36 = 64 → b = √64 = 8 m.

Cross-check: 6, 8, 10 is just the 3-4-5 triple doubled. ✓

A rectangle's diagonal cuts it into two right-angled triangles. The diagonal is the hypotenuse; length and width are the short sides.

d = √(length² + width²)

Example: a rectangle is 9 cm by 12 cm. Find the diagonal.

d² = 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 → d = 15 cm.

(Another 3-4-5 family triangle: 9, 12, 15.)

mcqs.q: Hypotenuse = 17, one short side = 8. What is the other short side?
To find a missing SHORT side, you should:
options: Add the squares of the other two sides
Subtract the smaller square from the larger square

numericals.q: A rectangle measures 6 cm by 8 cm. What is the length of its diagonal, in cm?

free_texts.q: After computing c² − a² to find a short side, the final operation you do is to take the ____ root. One word.
